newsitem.title: UK: Europe's AI(R) confirms in talks with S.Koreans.
newsitem.headline: Europe's AI(R) confirms in talks with S.Koreans.

text.p: Europe's Aero International(Regional) consortium said on Friday that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with a group of South Korean firms about their joining its $1 billion project to develop a 70-seat short-range airliner. AI(R) said in a statement released here that the MOU was signed "to define the principles which could eventually lead to a future industrial partnership in the AI(R)Jet project".

Earlier South Korea's trade ministry had announced that the 14-member Korean Commercial Aircraft Development Consortium (KCDC) had agreed to take a minimum 30 percent stake in the project and a final contract was expected within the next three months.
KCDC is led by Samsung Aerospace Industries Co and includes Korean Air Lines Co, Daewoo Heavy Industries Co and Hyundai Space and Aircraft Co.

AI(R) was formed two years ago by France's Aerospatiale, Finmeccanica unit Alenia of Italy and British Aerospace to combine sales and support operations for their existing ATR, Jetstream and Avro RJ aircraft.

AI(R) has been seeking risk-sharing partners for the new AI(R)Jet aircraft and held a conference for prospective subcontractors at its headquarters in Toulouse in January to invite them to buy into the project.
It said up to 50 percent of aerostructures work on the new aircraft would be available to investors, leaving the other half for AI(R)'s founding shareholders.

The company said on Friday that KCDC was one of the participants at the January conference and it was also continuing negotiations with other firms "in order to rapidly define the overall AI(R)Jet programme partnership".
